top_choice_rationale: P001 (Car and Parrinello) rests on one dated, physically transparent step, the 1985 extended Lagrangian that propagates electrons and nuclei together, in a two-author paper with no credit dispute and no pressure on the three-laureate limit. Four decades of independent use in proton transfer, liquid water and condensed-phase reactions fix its interpretation, and a citation limited to the 1985 unification avoids adjudicating later metadynamics or machine-learned potentials. The category and third-computational-prize concerns are real but answerable. P002 follows for its mechanistic pKa-switching and encapsulation concept, though its three-name credit cut is contestable; P003 is mature and clean but a follow-on to the 2010 cross-coupling prize; awarding nothing is least preferred.
